newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to study pork exports to 13 nations.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to study pork exports to 13 nations.

text.p: Taiwan trade officials said on Tuesday they were exploring new overseas markets for Taiwan pork in a bid to cope with a devastating hog epidemic that has wiped out the island's huge exports to Japan.
"We are working through our overseas offices in 13 countries to understand their needs and their concerns about Taiwan pork," an official of the cabinet's Board of Foreign Trade said by telephone.

Taiwan on March 20 banned pork exports and ordered a mass slaughter and inoculation drive after confirming an outbreak of the deadly contagious foot-and-mouth disease at nine hog farms -- a number that since has exploded to nearly 2,500 farms.
Japan and South Korea have explicitly banned pork imports from Taiwan. The Philippines has forbidden imports of meat from any cloven-hoofed animal in Taiwan.

The official said there was no plan to lift the export ban and that no country had agreed to buy Taiwan pork, but officials were focusing on 13 overseas markets as potential importers in hopes of easing local inventories and boosting prices.
They include Vietnam, Malaysia, Italy and Britain, he said.
An official of the cabinet's Council of Agriculture said it was unlikely that any of the 13 would agree to import Taiwan pork before the island's own export ban is lifted.
"We must make sure our pork is 100 percent safe for export and then ease the ban before others will consider it," farm council official Liao An-ting told Reuters by telephone.
The airborne virus has been detected on 2,469 of Taiwan's 25,000 hog farms, with officials projecting that 2.16 million of the island's 14 million pigs would have to be destroyed.
Farmers and soldiers were slaughtering all hogs -- healthy or otherwise -- at all farms hit by the virus, while all cloven-hoofed livestock were being vaccinated at healthy farms.
Analysts say the epidemic could shave as much as one percentage point off Taiwan's gross domestic product growth in 1997, a major setback to its hard-won economic recovery.
